title: fixture: BH-9441 body (client names replaced)
body:
HOTFIX: the in-build review approves PRs that the lead review then blocks on plain spec gaps.

## Problem

- Lead and security BLOCK findings in 14 days, by distinct ticket: wrong-data 88 (widget-fixture 41, cromford 33, gadget-fixture-os 12), red-build 59, core-flow-broken 41, data-loss 25, auth-bypass 16, money 11.
- The blocks are ticket requirements the diff does not deliver, which the in-build review had approved:
  - widget-fixture#3322 (WF-3178): "ticket asks for time in a state ... the kind measures time since createdAt".
  - widget-fixture#3140: "rows do not have the `name` field. Ticket Scope 4 asks...".
  - widget-fixture#3198 (WF-1394): "[BLOCK wrong-data] write-grant.ts:36 ... for every existing user this does not work".
- 36 PRs were abandoned on "findings outlasted the fix round". 20 carry a large-diff note (median about 2,900 lines; WF-1506 4,166 lines in 59 files; BH-7876 5,970 lines in 74 files). Their evidence claims are almost all "inconclusive" (29/29, 18/18, 16/16).
- CI failures from contracts the plan did not list: widget-fixture#3802 failed `tenancy-class.dt-1` because a new migration had no `-- tenancy:` header; cromford PRs fail `lanes-registry` when a lane is added without its catalog fragment.

## Scope (files: `prompts/stages/plan.md`, `prompts/stages/review.md`, `prompts/lead-review-checklist.md`, plan and review gates in `bin/lib/rb/`)

1. PLAN: "## Requirements coverage" has one row per ticket noun, field and number, each quoted from the ticket, with the file and the test that deliver it. A gate refuses a plan whose coverage table has fewer rows than the ticket has scope items.
2. PLAN: a "## Shared contracts" section. Each repo declares its contracts in a fragment directory in the repo (for example: a new migration needs a tenancy header; a new lane needs a `catalog/lanes.d` fragment; a new tool needs its registry fragment). The plan lists each contract the diff triggers, and EXECUTE adds it. The verification-map render carries the list to the plan stage.
3. REVIEW (in-build): run the lead-review checklist lens (`prompts/lead-review-checklist.md`) in the build, row by row against the coverage table. A row with no delivering code is `[BLOCK wrong-data]` or `[BLOCK core-flow-broken]` in the build, where a fix pass is cheap.
4. Evidence: a build whose evidence claims are all "inconclusive" does not report APPROVE; it reports the claims it could not prove as `[NOTE] not verified here` and names the reason (no database, no browser).
5. Measure: add to the daily digest the share of PRs where the lead review blocked after an in-build APPROVE. State the 14-day baseline in the PR.

## Acceptance tests (red first)

- prompt-eval golden scenarios: a ticket with 4 scope items and a plan with 3 coverage rows is refused; a fixture diff that lacks a ticket field gets a BLOCK from the in-build review.
- A fixture migration with no tenancy header: the plan lists the contract.
- An all-inconclusive evidence block does not produce APPROVE.
- No test calls a model outside the eval lane.

## Entry points

no user-facing entry point

## Out of scope

The size gate limits (#6025, a decision for the operator) and the ticket slicing rule (#8739).

Source: a read of 14 days of `logs/merge-conductor.log`, `logs/blocked-resolver.log`, `logs/findings.log`, the build dirs and `state/merge-conductor/` on the hub (2026-10-27 to 2026-11-10). Check each cause in code before the build. Report: `docs/MERGE_FAILURES_2026-11-10.html`.
